comment: Replicated. Three in-domain lone-C runs of mine, each with the paper's predict() at error at or below 0.03 (bar 3 x 0.01): 2026-11-19/r1/lab-vernier/003 (at rest, T=20, error 0.0049), 2026-11-19/r3/lab-vernier/001 (speed 3.69, T=40, error 0.0049), and 2026-11-20/r1/lab-vernier/001 (start (8.5,1.5), velocity (2.0,-3.5), T=40, several wall reflections, error 0.0049). All three match at tracker-noise level (about 0.005 for an exact model). Domain as claimed: one species-C particle. Note on the domain: a lone particle passes the numeric domain test vacuously, so these runs test free flight with walls, which is what P-0002 claims. They do not test any pair force. This review replaces the interim one.
